plan: Candidate 0007 is a minimal child of 0006's non-autocast Triton CE branch. The only change: eliminate the separate logits.float() conversion launch in _FusedCrossEntropy.forward. 0005/0006 materialized probabilities = logits.float() (a full extra device launch producing an FP32 copy) and then had the forward kernel read AND write that same FP32 buffer. 0007 instead (a) for low-precision/BF16 input allocates a fresh uninitialized FP32 probability buffer with torch.empty_like(dtype=float32) — no conversion launch — and lets the fused forward kernel load the BF16 logits directly and widen them to FP32 in-kernel, writing softmax into the separate FP32 buffer; (b) for FP32 input aliases the input itself as the probability buffer so the native observable in-place softmax overwrite is preserved. The forward kernel gains a distinct read pointer (LOGITS, native dtype) and write pointer (PROB, FP32). Because BF16->FP32 widening is exact and both torch.float() and tl.to(tl.float32) perform the same lossless widening, the FP32 value entering the max/exp/sum/log math is bitwise identical to the parent, so loss and softmax outputs are unchanged; only the extra .float() launch is removed. The process-local compiled-code cache key for the forward now additionally encodes logits.dtype and prob.dtype (plus existing device/vocab/block/alignment) so the BF16-read and FP32-read compilations never collide. Backward, the autocast native-equivalent Torch branch, the int64 wide-label handling, the gradient-alias behavior, the residual/RMSNorm prefix and every entry point remain byte-identical to 0006. Scope stays TP=1, zero smoothing, seq128/vocab1024 as tested; seq256/512 and vocab4096/8192 are not claimed.
lineage: 0007 <- 0006 <- 0005 <- 0004 <- 0003 (residual/RMSNorm fusion) <- 0002. 0007 is a minimal child of the promoted 0006 modifying ONLY the non-autocast Triton CE forward: it removes the separate logits.float() conversion launch from _FusedCrossEntropy.forward and _ce_forward_kernel by loading native-dtype logits directly and widening to FP32 in-kernel into a separate FP32 probability buffer (fresh buffer for BF16, aliased input for FP32). Forward launch cache key gains logits.dtype and prob.dtype. Backward, autocast native-equivalent Torch branch (0006), int64 wide-label handling (0005), gradient-alias behavior, residual/RMSNorm prefix (0003) and all public entry points are byte-identical to 0006.
semantic_risks: BF16->FP32 widening is exact, so loss/softmax are expected bitwise-identical to 0006; any observed divergence would indicate the vendor Triton 2.1.0 build widens BF16 loads differently than torch.float() (must be checked on the actual BI-V150 CoreX 4.2 runner, not assumed).

The fresh FP32 probability buffer is torch.empty_like(dtype=float32); every lane col<V is written by the masked store so the [S,B,V] buffer is fully initialized, but any future vocab-padding change that leaves lanes in [0,V) unwritten would read uninitialized memory in backward.

For FP32 input the probability buffer aliases the input, so the forward softmax overwrite mutates the input in place and the returned gradient aliases the input storage; this intentionally matches native gradient-alias/observable-mutation behavior but means an FP32 caller that re-reads its logits tensor after the call sees softmax, not logits.

The forward now relies on in-kernel read-from-LOGITS / write-to-PROB with LOGITS==PROB in the FP32-alias case; correctness depends on each program fully reducing its row into registers before the first store, which holds for the single-row-per-program BLOCK layout but would break if the kernel were later retiled to write before completing the row reduction.

Removing the .float() launch changes the device launch sequence; the compiled-code cache now distinguishes BF16-read vs FP32-read compilations by dtype keys, but if the adapter ever passes FP16 logits the exact-widening argument still holds while the autocast/dtype guards remain the adapter's responsibility.
Scope remains TP=1, zero smoothing, tested seq128/vocab1024; seq256/512 and vocab4096/8192 are untested and not claimed.
